newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Nigerians to investigate Sierra Leone coup plot.
newsitem.headline: Nigerians to investigate Sierra Leone coup plot.

text.p: Sierra Leone has invited investigators from Nigeria for an independent probe into an alleged attempt to topple the elected government in Freetown this month, radio Sierra Leone said on Wednesday.

It said Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha had agreed to send 15 of his crack investigators this week following a request from President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah. Officials said Kabbah, who took power from military rulers last March, was to have been killed in the September 8 foiled coup.
Five soldiers have been detained over the alleged attempt, the fifth arrested only on Tuesday, according to authorities.
"It is important for all the elements in the case to be brought out so that those identified with the coup plot will face justice," the state-owned radio said.

Diplomats say Kabbah's decision to call in outside investigators may have been prompted by growing talk that the coup plot may have been invented to cover up the government's inability to halt Sierra Leone's economic slide.
Nigeria is the regional military power and its troops are backing the government army in the five-year guerrilla war in Sierra Leone, a fellow Anglophone country.

But the choice of its investigators surprised many diplomats in Freetown. Nigeria provoked international outcry last year when it passed death sentences on some of about 40 accused coup plotters, including former head of state Olusegun Obasanjo.
Many Nigerians and foreign critics said the plot was fabricated.

Worldwide protest forced Abacha to commute the death sentences to life terms. His government, however, plunged into international opprobrium again by hanging nine activists including writer Ken Saro-Wiwa last November on charges of murder.
